text:
Claude Giroux is 38 and spent Thursday doing something he's done all his career: scoring on the Flyers, now as the visitor. He deflected a point shot early in Philadelphia, his 1,000 games there long behind him, and the Senators lost 6-5 in overtime anyway.

The scoring line (5 goals, 13 points in 23 games) looks like a veteran easing down. The five-on-five line says otherwise. Ottawa takes 60.3% of the expected goals with him on the ice, and he's 8.3 points better than the team without him, one of the best marks on the roster. His linemates simply haven't finished: the on-ice goals sit about four below what the chances deserved, so his assists are the likeliest number on this page to climb. Evolving-Hockey had the same profile last season: 2.1 wins, 47th among forwards, with opponents getting fewer chances when he played.

He's a passer more than a shooter now, and he barely touches the power play (one point). What to watch: whether Travis Green keeps trusting him with 16 to 19 minutes, because the process says he's earning them.
